title: The letter about the rent
text: A letter from {~the agency|your landlord|the letting office} says the rent is going up. {~It calls this 'an adjustment in line with the market'.|The word 'unfortunately' appears twice.|It arrived on a Friday, which felt deliberate.}

outcomes.text: I paid. There was a week of grumbling and then it was just the rent.
The new rent ate the gap I had been saving for. I stopped buying lunch out.
I showed {~the damp|the ageing boiler|three cheaper listings} and they came down to half of what they'd asked.
They said the increase was non-negotiable. I felt like I had asked for something rude.
They said no, then mentioned that the owner was 'considering options'. Nothing good follows that sentence.
I spent three weekends at viewings. One flat smelled of cabbage and had a bath in the kitchen.
I found something cheaper and smaller, and moved before the increase took effect.

title: A patch on the wall
text: There is a dark patch spreading {~behind the wardrobe|in the corner of the bedroom|above the window} and the air has started to smell of wet {~wool|cardboard|earth}.

choices.label: Photograph it and write to the landlord

outcomes.text: A man came and sprayed something on it. It came back within the month, but I had a paper trail.
The landlord's reply said it was condensation and suggested I open a window. I opened a window.
They sent a proper builder. It took a week and the flat smelt of paint, but the wall is finally dry.
I spent a Sunday with bleach and a mask. It helped, and I coughed for two days.
The patch returned a week later and the bleach smell stayed a month.
I hung a picture over it. The picture started to curl.
I developed a cough that took a doctor three appointments to link to the wall.

title: No hot water
text: The boiler {~gave a long groan and died|started clicking and then stopped|went out in the middle of a shower} and the flat is cold enough to see your breath in.

outcomes.text: {~An engineer came the next day|The landlord sent someone within the week}. The new boiler is enormous and quiet.
Six weeks of cold showers and emails. Eventually a man came with a part the size of a biscuit.
The landlord told me to 'call the manufacturer'. The manufacturer told me to call the landlord.
The engineer was kind and the bill wasn't. I got the money back out of the next rent after an argument.
I paid and never saw the money again. The landlord said 'noted'.

choices.label: Stay with a friend until it's sorted

outcomes.text: A week on someone's sofa reminded me who my friends were. They wouldn't take a penny.
The week on a sofa became a month, and we both started to count the days.

title: An inspection
text: {~Your landlord|The agency} has given you forty-eight hours' notice of an inspection. The flat has not been tidy since {~March|the spring|you moved in}.

outcomes.text: The place passed. The landlord ran a finger along a shelf and looked almost disappointed.
I found two things I'd lost months ago and a third I'd hoped was gone for good.
It was enough. I was told the place 'was well kept', which is the nicest thing anyone has said about it.
They opened a cupboard. The cupboard did not behave.
Legally, I was right. The landlord's face did not agree, and the repairs I'd asked for stopped being urgent.
They backed down with an email the length of a legal threat. I kept the flat; I lost some goodwill.

title: The deposit
text: {~The landlord is deducting|The agency says it will be keeping} a large part of your deposit for 'wear beyond fair use': a scuff, a carpet, and something called 'professional cleaning'.

outcomes.text: I'd photographed everything on move-in day. The scheme ruled in my favour and I got most of it back.
It took four months and a form for every wall. I won half.
I was tired. I let them have it and moved on.
I accepted and then found a stain on the paperwork I hadn't noticed. Too late.
The judge barely looked at the landlord's folder. I won, and my mother framed the letter.
The landlord didn't turn up and the case was adjourned twice. It still ended in my favour, eventually.
I lost on a technicality involving a missing signature. I have never read a lease so carefully.

title: The flatmate is late with the rent
text: {~Your flatmate|The person you share with} is short again this month and has a very good reason, which is different from last month's.

outcomes.text: They paid me back in instalments and a lasagne. I have mixed feelings about the lasagne.
They never mentioned it again. Neither did I, out loud.
We made a schedule and a rule, and the next three months went better than the last three.
It turned into an argument about the dishes, and then about everything, and then about nothing.
The landlord sorted it out with a letter. Our flat has been silent since, like a library with grievances.
The flatmate moved out that weekend, leaving the fridge full of mystery leftovers.

title: They have people round
text: It's {~a Tuesday|midnight|a work night} and your flatmate's {~friends have arrived|birthday has begun|'quiet evening' has become a DJ set}.

outcomes.text: I met someone I'd never have spoken to otherwise. We exchanged numbers. The hangover was memorable.
At 3 a.m. I was the one sitting on the stairs explaining my life to a stranger called Doug.

choices.label: Go to bed and put earplugs in

outcomes.text: It worked until the smoke alarm. I slept through the music and woke up to the fire brigade.
The earplugs held. I woke up fresh, and the kitchen looked like a crime scene.

choices.label: Tell them to turn it down

outcomes.text: They did, graciously, and thanked me for being direct.
They turned it up, slightly. We didn't speak for a week.
The neighbours called the landlord and I got the letter.

title: The lease is up
text: The lease on {~the flat|your place} runs out next month and {~the agency|your landlord} would like to know what you intend to do.

outcomes.text: A year's security, at a price. I hung the pictures I'd been putting off.
They wanted a higher rent and a clause about pets I didn't read until later.
It costs a little more and I keep my options open. I never quite relax.
They said yes, and then sold the building three months later.

choices.label: Walk away and find somewhere new

outcomes.text: I found a flat with a view of a car park and a landlord who replies to messages. I'll take it.
I searched for weeks and nearly ended up on a sofa. The place I found smells of someone else's dinners.

title: Locked out
text: It's {~eleven at night|raining|the coldest night of the year} and your keys are on the kitchen table, on the other side of a door.

outcomes.text: A man arrived in twelve minutes and opened the door in four. The bill was more than my shoes.
The locksmith was a scam. He charged three times the quote and left the door broken.

choices.label: Wake the neighbour with the spare

outcomes.text: They'd been asleep for an hour and still made me tea. I owe them a bottle of wine.
They weren't in. I sat on the stairs for three hours until a flatmate came home.
I got in without a scratch, and was enormously pleased with myself.
I got in with a split lip and a bruised pride. The neighbour filmed it.
The police were called by someone who thought I was a burglar. Explaining myself took an hour.

title: The first place that was yours
text: {~Your first flat|The first place with your name on the lease} has a mattress, one chair and a window that opens onto {~a brick wall|a neighbour's washing|a wonderful slice of sky}.

choices.label: Spend a weekend making it home

outcomes.text: I painted one wall a colour I'd never choose again. I slept like a child that night.
I found a plant, a lamp and a chair at a charity shop. The room started to have an opinion.
Everyone stood in the kitchen, as everyone does. It was the best night of my year.
Only two people came, and we ate all the crisps. It was oddly perfect.

choices.label: Live out of boxes for months

outcomes.text: The boxes became furniture. It was a long time before it felt like mine.
I got used to it, and then I stopped noticing I hadn't unpacked at all.

title: The first crash
text: {~You were reversing|You took a corner too fast|The road was wet and the car in front stopped suddenly}. There's a crunch, then a silence, then someone getting out of the other car.

outcomes.text: They were decent about it. The insurer was less decent, and the premium jumped.
The other driver turned out to be a neighbour's uncle. We've waved to each other ever since.
They had dashcam footage. I've never felt so small in a car park.
It went to the insurers, who split the blame, and my premium rose anyway.
I got four streets before I started shaking. Someone had taken my number plate.
I was caught on a doorbell camera, and two days later a police officer was sitting in the kitchen with my mother.

title: A ticket under the wiper
text: There's a yellow envelope under the windscreen wiper of your car. {~You were there for eleven minutes.|The sign was behind a tree.|You were sure that bay was free.}

outcomes.text: It was quicker than the alternative. I've since become very good at reading signs.
I paid the discounted rate and swore at an envelope.
The appeal was upheld. The warden had measured the wrong bay. I felt a disproportionate joy.
The appeal was rejected after six weeks, and the fine doubled.
It turned into a court letter. I paid it with the extra fee and my tail between my legs.
Nothing happened for a year, then a bailiff's letter arrived and I couldn't pretend any more.

title: The long way in
text: {~The journey takes over an hour|The commute has crept up again|You do the sums and lose a full working day every week}, each way, and you've started to hate {~the bridge|the ring road|the platform|the stop}.

outcomes.text: I found a place ten minutes away. It cost more, and every morning felt like a gift.
The flat was tiny and the noise was terrible, but I got back ten hours a week.
I started listening to books on the journey. A year later I'd read sixty.
I started learning a language. My accent on the platform was the talk of the carriage.
After a pilot, they agreed to two days a week. It changed everything.
They said the job needed 'presence'. The look on my face was noted.
They refused, and I started looking at other jobs.

title: The empty lock
text: You come out to the rack and find {~a cut lock|the lock, neatly snapped|nothing but a front wheel} where your bike was.

outcomes.text: The police gave me a crime number and an apologetic smile. I got nothing else from them.
A week later a patrol found it in a skip. It needed a new chain and a bit of grace.
The new one was better, and heavier, and I named it after my grandmother.
The new one was stolen within the year too. I've learned about locks.
I hate to admit I like it. Forty minutes of reading a book.
The bus turned out to be late every morning, and I missed the ride.

title: Cancelled
text: The board says {~CANCELLED|DELAYED|SIGNAL FAILURE}. The platform fills with people sighing in unison.

outcomes.text: Forty minutes later we crammed on. I stood with my face against someone's rucksack, reflecting.
It came, it was empty, and I got a seat. A small miracle.
I got a taxi with three strangers. We split the fare and became briefly close.
I walked the whole way and arrived an hour late, cold and strangely proud.

choices.label: Go home and say you'll work from home

outcomes.text: My boss said 'sure', in a tone that I thought about all day.
I got more done at the kitchen table than I'd done all week, and nobody noticed.

title: The stranger on the bus
text: {~Someone sits beside you|Someone across the aisle catches your eye} and says, unprompted, {~'You look like you've had a day.'|'Is this seat taken?'|'That book is terrible, by the way.'}

outcomes.text: We talked for four stops. I never saw them again, and think about them most weeks.
We swapped numbers. They became a friend, of the kind you only have on certain days of the week.
Sometimes the best conversation is the one you don't have. I got home rested.
I regretted it by my stop. There was something in their face I should have answered.
The next seat was worse, and next to someone eating curry.
It was awkward but fine.

title: The renewal quote
text: Your car insurance renewal has arrived and {~the number has changed|it's gone up again|the cheapest quote this year came from a company you've never heard of}.

outcomes.text: After forty minutes on comparison sites I saved enough to buy a very good dinner.
I found a cheaper deal, then found out why: the excess was enormous.
I paid it. Loyalty is an expensive habit.
I paid it and kept my no-claims bonus. A small comfort.
It saved money, and I spent the year holding my breath.
I dropped to basic cover, and a stone put a crack in my windscreen the next week.

title: The flash
text: {~A flash in the mirror|A grey box on a pole|A letter in a brown envelope} tells you that you were {~going a little faster than the sign suggested|doing 42 in a 30|thinking about something else}.

outcomes.text: I paid the fine and did the speed awareness course. The man running it was more entertaining than I'd feared.
I paid it and went on a course, learning that my road has a habit of catching people.
A technicality saved me. The camera hadn't been calibrated.
I went to court. The magistrate was not amused and the fine doubled.
It blew up in my face, and my cousin has stopped returning my calls.
It worked, and I spent the next year jumpy every time a letter arrived.

title: Someone you meant to call
text: You realise it has been {~four years|longer than you'd like to say|since before the last move} since you talked to an old friend, and neither of you did anything to cause it.

outcomes.text: They picked up on the second ring and said 'I was just thinking about you.' I don't know whether it was true.
It was awkward for about three minutes and then it wasn't. We made a plan for the summer.
The number had changed. I found them on social media. They were warm but distant.
I spent an hour writing it and ten seconds sending it. The reply came next morning: 'God, yes.'
No reply came. I've decided it's the silence of someone who is busy, rather than someone who isn't interested.
Some friendships are for a season. I thought about them on a bench once, and then I stopped.
Two years later I heard they had moved abroad. I felt the loss more than I'd expected.

title: The group chat
text: The group chat {~has 312 unread messages|went off at 2 a.m.|has turned into an argument about something none of you can now remember}.

outcomes.text: There was a real argument in there, with real feelings. I replied with something kind, for once.
Forty minutes of memes and one heartfelt message from someone who's struggling. I rang them.
Ah, peace. A week later I'd missed a birthday and a flat-warming.
The silence was wonderful. Nobody noticed. I'm not sure what that says.
Two people messaged to ask if I was okay. I wasn't sure how to answer.
Nobody said anything and it stung, though I'd done it myself.

title: Asked to say a few words
text: The family of {~someone you knew|an old friend|a person who mattered to you} has asked whether you would speak at the funeral. {~They say you were the one who knew them best.|You said yes before you'd thought about it.}

outcomes.text: I spent three nights on it. I read it out, and they laughed and cried, in that order.
The page shook in my hands. I finished, and sat down, and felt something open up in me.
It was messy and real. Someone told me afterwards it was the best eulogy they'd heard.
I got three sentences in and couldn't go on. Someone took my hand and finished the story.
Someone else spoke, well, and I sat at the back thinking about what I would have said.
I sent a letter for someone to read. It was kind, and it wasn't the same.

title: Dinner from scratch
text: You {~try a recipe you've been meaning to|decide to cook for the week|invite people over and promise a proper meal}, and the kitchen fills with smells.

outcomes.text: It came out tasting like the picture. I want that in writing.
It came out tasting like a photograph of the dish, and everyone was polite.
A handful of something I found in the cupboard turned out to be the secret. Everyone asked for the recipe.
The smoke alarm sang. We ordered pizza, and it was the best night of the month.
A delivery at nine. No regrets and a little guilt.
The delivery was wrong, cold and late, and I ate toast.

title: The takeaway bill
text: You look at the bank statement and there is a column of delivery apps that looks like {~a phone number|a list of small betrayals|someone else's life}.

outcomes.text: I bought a pan and an ambition. It wasn't good at first, and then it was.
I ate beans on toast for a fortnight and felt pure.
I told myself it was self-care. My waistband didn't agree.
A friend stared at me across a pile of cartons. I changed the subject.
I set an allowance and a rule. The rule lasted three weeks. The allowance lasted two.
It worked, for once. I was amazed at how small the budget really was.

title: A box of photographs
text: You find {~a shoebox|an album|a drawer of envelopes} of old photographs, the kind that {~smell of the chemist|have a thumbprint on the corner}.

choices.label: Spend the evening going through them

outcomes.text: There was one of you laughing that you had no memory of. I kept it on the fridge.
I found someone I had forgotten I loved. I put the photo down and stared at the wall for a while.
Three people cried, two argued about who was in the photograph. It was the best gift I've given.
It took a month, and nobody replied. I kept going, and I'm glad I did.
Some things are better in the dark. Not all, but some.
I meant to come back to them. I haven't.

title: No connection
text: The {~internet|wifi|line} has been down for {~two days|most of a week|long enough to notice}, and you've discovered how much of your life lives on it.

outcomes.text: After an hour on hold, a man named Darren talked me through turning it off and on again. It worked.
They promised an engineer between 8 and 6. He came at 5:55 and fixed it in a minute.

choices.label: Use it as an excuse to unplug

outcomes.text: I read a book, took a walk and called my mother. It was the best weekend in a year.
By day two I was twitching. By day three I'd found a hobby.

choices.label: Go to the library or a cafe

outcomes.text: I worked in a cafe for three days, and had a conversation with the barista that I still remember.
Every seat was taken by someone on the same mission. We nodded like survivors.

title: The family meal
text: It's {~a holiday|Sunday|someone's birthday}, and the family are at the table. {~Nobody has sat down yet|The argument has already started|Someone has brought up politics}.

outcomes.text: I changed the subject three times and got away with a good dinner.
I kept the peace, but bit my tongue until it bled.
Silence fell. Then someone said 'he's right,' and the night turned around.
It ended with a slammed door and a cold plate of pudding in my lap.
The best conversation of the night was by the sink, over the dishes.
I dropped a dish and everyone looked at me. It was a happy accident, in the end.
